correctness.rationale: For every \(1\le p\le2\), normalized sign-coefficient Hölder duality and the scalar Hilbert numerical-radius polarization bound give \(w_p(\mathbf T)\ge(2k^{1/q})^{-1}\max_\varepsilon\|\sum_j\varepsilon_jT_j\|\). Exact averaging over all sign patterns proves \(\max_\varepsilon\|\sum_j\varepsilon_jT_j\|\ge\|\mathbf T\|_2\), and the finite-coordinate norm comparison yields \(\|\mathbf T\|_p\le k^{1/p-1/2}\|\mathbf T\|_2\). Together these give the sharp constant \((2\sqrt{k})^{-1}\). For \(p\ge2\), comparison with the largest individual operator norm gives \((2k^{1/p})^{-1}\). An explicit commuting square-zero common-source rank-one tuple attains both branches, including the endpoint \(p=1\). A separate checker passed 3283 deterministic assertions on exact sign averaging, polarization, algebraic exponents and finite witness inequalities. Finite experiments do not replace the universal analytic proof.

originality.rationale: The verified claim is the all-exponent sharp index for unrestricted complex Hilbert operator tuples under \(\dim H\ge k+1\). Mal (2022/2023) establishes \(p=2\) for \(k<\dim H\) and \(p>2\) only for \(k=2\), and his general p bound is strictly weaker below \(p=2\) for \(k>1\). Moslehian--Sattari--Shebrawi (2017) state a signed-combination Holder lower bound but not the sharp \(p<2\) index or rank-one attainment. The closest published Euclidean common-source result is explicitly restricted to \(p=2\) and rank-one tuples. No found literature statement or inspected stronger theorem directly entails the full low-p equality and phase law; some full-text access limitations and unindexed-equivalence risks remain.
residual_risks: The subscription-restricted full text of Cevik--Bhunia (2026) was not available; its more general p-inequalities could in principle imply the low-p result.
Drnovsek--Muller (2014) full text was not inspected; its accessible description focuses on Euclidean radius.
An unindexed signed-combination or 2-summing-operator theorem might yield a mathematically equivalent low-p constant without using joint-index terminology.
Search results and available prior records do not constitute a proof of global uniqueness.

value.rationale: This is an exact natural invariant for the complete \((p,k)\) family in complex Hilbert spaces above the sharp witness-dimension threshold, not a one-off norm computation. For \(1\le p<2\) and \(k>1\) the exact result strictly improves the published Mal general bound by factor \(k^{1/p-1/2}\), and its flat low-exponent regime and changing output-support extremizers expose a structural phase transition. Higher-p cases cohere in one sharp classification but are not used to inflate novelty beyond known lower bounds.
